Q.16.ans: God created all the angels<sup>f</sup> spirits,<sup>g</sup> immortal,<sup>h</sup> holy,<sup>i</sup> excelling in knowledge,<sup>k</sup> mighty in power,<sup>l</sup> to execute his commandments, and to praise his name,<sup>m</sup> yet subject to change.<sup>n</sup>

Q.17.ans: After God had made all other creatures, he created man male and female;<sup>o</sup> formed the body of the man of the dust of the ground,<sup>p</sup> and the woman of the rib of the man,<sup>q</sup> endued them with living, reasonable, and immortal souls;<sup>r</sup> made them after his own image,<sup>s</sup> in knowledge,<sup>t</sup> righteousness, and holiness;<sup>u</sup> having the law of God writ- ten in their hearts,<sup>w</sup> and power to fulfill it,<sup>x</sup> and dominion over the creatures;<sup>y</sup> yet subject to fall.<sup>z</sup>

Q.18.ans: God’s works of providence are his most holy,<sup>a</sup> wise,<sup>b</sup> and pow- erful preserving<sup>c</sup> and governing<sup>d</sup> all his creatures; ordering them, and all their actions,<sup>e</sup> to his own glory.<sup>f</sup>

Q.19.ans: God by his providence permitted some of the angels, willfully and irrecoverably, to fall into sin and damnation,<sup>g</sup> limiting and order- ing that, and all their sins, to his own glory;<sup>h</sup> and established the rest in holiness and happiness;<sup>i</sup> employing them all,<sup>k</sup> at his pleasure, in the administrations of his power, mercy, and justice.<sup>l</sup>

Q.20.ans: The providence of God toward man in the estate in which he was created, was the placing him in paradise, appointing him to dress it, giving him liberty to eat of the fruit of the earth;<sup>m</sup> putting the creatures under his dominion,<sup>n</sup> and ordaining marriage for his help;<sup>o</sup> affording him communion with himself;<sup>p</sup> instituting the Sabbath;<sup>q</sup> entering into a covenant of life with him, upon condition of per- sonal, perfect, and perpetual obedience,<sup>r</sup> of which the tree of life was a pledge;<sup>s</sup> and forbidding to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, upon the pain of death.<sup>t</sup>

Q.21.ans: Our first parents being left to the freedom of their own will, through the temptation of Satan, transgressed the commandment of God in eating the forbidden fruit; and thereby fell from the estate of innocency wherein they were created.<sup>u</sup>

Q.22.ans: The covenant being made with Adam as a public person, not for himself only, but for his posterity, all mankind descending from him by ordinary generation,<sup>w</sup> sinned in him, and fell with him in that first transgression.<sup>x</sup>

Q.23.ans: The fall brought mankind into an estate of sin and misery.<sup>y</sup>

Q.24.ans: Sin is any want of conformity unto, or transgression of, any law of God, given as a rule to the reasonable creature.<sup>z</sup>

Q.25.ans: The sinfulness of that estate whereinto man fell, consisteth in the guilt of Adam’s first sin,<sup>a</sup> the want of that righteousness wherein he was created, and the corruption of his nature, whereby he is ut- terly indisposed, disabled, and made opposite unto all that is spiritu- ally good, and wholly inclined to all evil, and that continually;<sup>b</sup> which is commonly called original sin, and from which do proceed all ac- tual transgressions.<sup>c</sup>

Q.26.ans: Original sin is conveyed from our first parents unto their pos- terity by natural generation, so as all that proceed from them in that way are conceived and born in sin.<sup>d</sup>

Q.27.ans: The fall brought upon mankind the loss of communion with God,<sup>e</sup> his displeasure and curse;<sup>f</sup> so as we are by nature children of wrath,<sup>g</sup> bond slaves to Satan,<sup>h</sup> and justly liable to all punishments in this world, and that which is to come.<sup>i</sup>

Q.28.ans: The punishments of sin in this world are either inward, as blindness of mind,<sup>k</sup> a reprobate sense,<sup>l</sup> strong delusions,<sup>m</sup> hardness of heart,<sup>n</sup> horror of conscience,<sup>o</sup> and vile affections;<sup>p</sup> or outward, as the curse of God upon the creatures for our sakes,<sup>q</sup> and all other evils that befall us in our bodies, names, estates, relations, and employ- ments;<sup>r</sup> together with death itself.<sup>s</sup>

Q.29.ans: The punishments of sin in the world to come, are everlasting separation from the comfortable presence of God, and most griev- ous torments in soul and body, without intermission, in hellfire forever.<sup>t</sup>

Q.30.ans: God doth not leave all men to perish in the estate of sin and misery,<sup>u</sup> into which they fell by the breach of the first covenant, com- monly called the covenant of works;<sup>w</sup> but of his mere love and mercy delivereth his elect out of it, and bringeth them into an estate of salvation by the second covenant, commonly called the covenant of grace.<sup>x</sup>

Q.31.ans: The covenant of grace was made with Christ as the second Adam, and in him with all the elect as his seed.<sup>y</sup>

Q.32.ans: The grace of God is manifested in the second covenant, in that he freely provideth and offereth to sinners a Mediator,<sup>z</sup> and life and salvation by him;<sup>a</sup> and requiring faith as the condition to interest them in him,<sup>b</sup> promiseth and giveth his Holy Spirit<sup>c</sup> to all his elect, to work in them that faith,<sup>d</sup> with all other saving graces;<sup>e</sup> and to enable them unto all holy obedience,<sup>f</sup> as the evidence of the truth of their faith<sup>g</sup> and thankfulness to God,<sup>h</sup> and as the way which he hath ap- pointed them to salvation.<sup>i</sup>

Q.33.ans: The covenant of grace was not always administered after the same manner, but the administrations of it under the old testament were different from those under the new.<sup>k</sup>

Q.34.ans: The covenant of grace was administered under the old testa- ment, by promises,<sup>l</sup> prophecies,<sup>m</sup> sacrifices,<sup>n</sup> circumcision,<sup>o</sup> the Passover,<sup>p</sup> and other types and ordinances, which did all foresignify Christ then to come, and were for that time sufficient to build up the elect in faith in the promised Messiah,<sup>q</sup> by whom they then had full remission of sin, and eternal salvation.<sup>r</sup>

Q.35.ans: Under the new testament, when Christ the substance was ex- hibited, the same covenant of grace was and still is to be adminis- tered in the preaching of the Word,<sup>s</sup> and the administration of the sacraments of baptism<sup>t</sup> and the Lord’s Supper;<sup>u</sup> in which grace and salvation are held forth in more fullness, evidence, and efficacy, to all nations.<sup>w</sup>

Q.36.ans: The only Mediator of the covenant of grace is the Lord Jesus Christ,<sup>x</sup> who, being the eternal Son of God, of one substance and equal with the Father,<sup>y</sup> in the fullness of time became man,<sup>z</sup> and so was and continues to be God and man, in two entire distinct natures, and one person, forever.<sup>a</sup>
groups: John 1:1, 14, 18, John 10:30, Phil 2:6, Ps 2:7, Matt 3:17, Matt 17:5

Q.37.ans: Christ the Son of God became man, by taking to himself a true body, and a reasonable soul,<sup>b</sup> being conceived by the power of the Holy Ghost in the womb of the virgin Mary, of her substance, and born of her,<sup>c</sup> yet without sin.<sup>d</sup>

Q.38.ans: It was requisite that the Mediator should be God, that he might sustain and keep the human nature from sinking under the infinite wrath of God, and the power of death;<sup>e</sup> give worth and efficacy to his sufferings, obedience, and intercession;<sup>f</sup> and to satisfy God’s justice,<sup>g</sup> procure his favor,<sup>h</sup> purchase a peculiar people,<sup>i</sup> give his Spirit to them,<sup>k</sup> conquer all their enemies,<sup>l</sup> and bring them to everlasting salvation.<sup>m</sup>

Q.39.ans: It was requisite that the Mediator should be man, that he might advance our nature,<sup>n</sup> perform obedience to the law,<sup>o</sup> suffer and make intercession for us in our nature,<sup>p</sup> have a fellow feeling of our infirmities;<sup>q</sup> that we might receive the adoption of sons,<sup>r</sup> and have comfort and access with boldness unto the throne of grace.<sup>s</sup>

Q.40.ans: It was requisite that the Mediator, who was to reconcile God and man, should himself be both God and man, and this in one person, that the proper works of each nature might be accepted of God for us,<sup>t</sup> and relied on by us, as the works of the whole person.<sup>u</sup>

Q.41.ans: Our Mediator was called Jesus, because he saveth his people from their sins.<sup>w</sup>

Q.42.ans: Our Mediator was called Christ, because he was anointed with the Holy Ghost above measure;<sup>x</sup> and so set apart, and fully furnished with all authority and ability,<sup>y</sup> to execute the offices of prophet,<sup>z</sup> priest,<sup>a</sup> and king of his church,<sup>b</sup> in the estate both of his humiliation and exaltation.

Q.43.ans: Christ executeth the office of a prophet, in his revealing to the church,<sup>c</sup> in all ages, by his Spirit and Word,<sup>d</sup> in divers ways of administration,<sup>e</sup> the whole will of God,<sup>f</sup> in all things concerning their edification and salvation.<sup>g</sup>

Q.44.ans: Christ executeth the office of a priest, in his once offering him- self a sacrifice without spot to God,<sup>h</sup> to be a reconciliation for the sins of his people;<sup>i</sup> and in making continual intercession for them.<sup>k</sup>

Q.45.ans: Christ executeth the office of a king, in calling out of the world a people to himself,<sup>l</sup> and giving them officers,<sup>m</sup> laws,<sup>n</sup> and censures, by which he visibly governs them;<sup>o</sup> in bestowing saving grace upon his elect,<sup>p</sup> rewarding their obedience,<sup>q</sup> and correcting them for their sins,<sup>r</sup> preserving and supporting them under all their temptations and sufferings,<sup>s</sup> restraining and overcoming all their enemies,<sup>t</sup> and power- fully ordering all things for his own glory,<sup>u</sup> and their good;<sup>w</sup> and also in taking vengeance on the rest, who know not God, and obey not the gospel.<sup>x</sup>

Q.46.ans: The estate of Christ’s humiliation was that low condition, wherein he for our sakes, emptying himself of his glory, took upon him the form of a servant,<sup>y</sup> in his conception<sup>z</sup> and birth,<sup>a</sup> life,<sup>b</sup> death,<sup>c</sup> and after his death,<sup>d</sup> until his resurrection.<sup>e</sup>

Q.47.ans: Christ humbled himself in his conception and birth, in that, being from all eternity the Son of God, in the bosom of the Father, he was pleased in the fullness of time to become the son of man, made of a woman of low estate, and to be born of her; with divers circumstances of more than ordinary abasement.<sup>f</sup>

Q.48.ans: Christ humbled himself in his life, by subjecting himself to the law,<sup>g</sup> which he perfectly fulfilled;<sup>h</sup> and by conflicting with the indigni- ties of the world,<sup>i</sup> temptations of Satan,<sup>k</sup> and infirmities in his flesh, whether common to the nature of man, or particularly accompany- ing that his low condition.<sup>l</sup>

Q.49.ans: Christ humbled himself in his death, in that having been be- trayed by Judas,<sup>m</sup> forsaken by his disciples,<sup>n</sup> scorned and rejected by the world,<sup>o</sup> condemned by Pilate, and tormented by his persecutors;<sup>p</sup> having also conflicted with the terrors of death, and the powers of darkness, felt and borne the weight of God’s wrath,<sup>q</sup> he laid down his life an offering for sin,<sup>r</sup> enduring the painful, shameful, and cursed death of the cross.<sup>s</sup>

Q.50.ans: Christ’s humiliation after his death consisted in his being buried,<sup>t</sup> and continuing in the state of the dead, and under the power of death till the third day;<sup>u</sup> which hath been otherwise expressed in these words, He descended into hell.

Q.51.ans: The estate of Christ’s exaltation comprehendeth his resurrec- tion,<sup>w</sup> ascension,<sup>x</sup> sitting at the right hand of the Father,<sup>y</sup> and his coming again to judge the world.<sup>z</sup>

Q.52.ans: Christ was exalted in his resurrection, in that, not having seen corruption in death, (of which it was not possible for him to be held,<sup>a</sup> ) and having the very same body in which he suffered, with the essen- tial properties thereof,<sup>b</sup> (but without mortality, and other common infirmities belonging to this life,) really united to his soul,<sup>c</sup> he rose again from the dead the third day by his own power;<sup>d</sup> whereby he declared himself to be the Son of God,<sup>e</sup> to have satisfied divine justice,<sup>f</sup> to have vanquished death, and him that had the power of it,<sup>g</sup> and to be Lord of quick and dead:<sup>h</sup> all which he did as a public person,<sup>i</sup> the head of his church,<sup>k</sup> for their justification,<sup>l</sup> quickening in grace,<sup>m</sup> support against enemies,<sup>n</sup> and to assure them of their resurrection from the dead at the last day.<sup>o</sup>

Q.53.ans: Christ was exalted in his ascension, in that having after his resurrection often appeared unto and conversed with his apostles, speaking to them of the things pertaining to the kingdom of God,<sup>p</sup> and giving them commission to preach the gospel to all nations,<sup>q</sup> forty days after his resurrection, he, in our nature, and as our head,<sup>r</sup> triumphing over enemies,<sup>s</sup> visibly went up into the highest heavens, there to receive gifts for men,<sup>t</sup> to raise up our affections thither,<sup>u</sup> and to prepare a place for us,<sup>w</sup> where himself is, and shall continue till his second coming at the end of the world.<sup>x</sup>

Q.54.ans: Christ is exalted in his sitting at the right hand of God, in that as God-man he is advanced to the highest favor with God the Father,<sup>y</sup> with all fullness of joy,<sup>z</sup> glory,<sup>a</sup> and power over all things in heaven and earth;<sup>b</sup> and doth gather and defend his church, and subdue their enemies; furnisheth his ministers and people with gifts and graces,<sup>c</sup> and maketh intercession for them.<sup>d</sup>

Q.55.ans: Christ maketh intercession, by his appearing in our nature continually before the Father in heaven,<sup>e</sup> in the merit of his obedi- ence and sacrifice on earth,<sup>f</sup> declaring his will to have it applied to all believers;<sup>g</sup> answering all accusations against them,<sup>h</sup> and procuring for them quiet of conscience, notwithstanding daily failings,<sup>i</sup> access with boldness to the throne of grace,<sup>k</sup> and acceptance of their persons<sup>l</sup> and services.<sup>m</sup>

Q.56.ans: Christ is to be exalted in his coming again to judge the world, in that he, who was unjustly judged and condemned by wicked men,<sup>n</sup> shall come again at the last day in great power,<sup>o</sup> and in the full mani- festation of his own glory, and of his Father’s, with all his holy angels,<sup>p</sup> with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trumpet of God,<sup>q</sup> to judge the world in righteousness.<sup>r</sup>

Q.57.ans: Christ, by his mediation, hath procured redemption,<sup>s</sup> with all other benefits of the covenant of grace.<sup>t</sup>

Q.58.ans: We are made partakers of the benefits which Christ hath pro- cured, by the application of them unto us,<sup>u</sup> which is the work espe- cially of God the Holy Ghost.<sup>w</sup>

Q.59.ans: Redemption is certainly applied, and effectually communi- cated, to all those for whom Christ hath purchased it;<sup>x</sup> who are in time by the Holy Ghost enabled to believe in Christ according to the gospel.<sup>y</sup>

Q.60.ans: They who, having never heard the gospel,<sup>z</sup> know not Jesus Christ,<sup>a</sup> and believe not in him, cannot be saved,<sup>b</sup> be they never so diligent to frame their lives according to the light of nature,<sup>c</sup> or the laws of that religion which they profess;<sup>d</sup> neither is there salvation in any other, but in Christ alone,<sup>e</sup> who is the Savior only of his body the church.<sup>f</sup>

Q.61.ans: All that hear the gospel, and live in the visible church, are not saved; but they only who are true members of the church invisible.<sup>g</sup>

Q.62.ans: The visible church is a society made up of all such as in all ages and places of the world do profess the true religion,<sup>h</sup> and of their children.<sup>i</sup>

Q.63.ans: The visible church hath the privilege of being under God’s special care and government;<sup>k</sup> of being protected and preserved in all ages, notwithstanding the opposition of all enemies;<sup>l</sup> and of en- joying the communion of saints, the ordinary means of salvation,<sup>m</sup> and offers of grace by Christ to all the members of it in the ministry of the gospel, testifying, that whosoever believes in him shall be saved,<sup>n</sup> and excluding none that will come unto him.<sup>o</sup>

Q.64.ans: The invisible church is the whole number of the elect, that have been, are, or shall be gathered into one under Christ the head.<sup>p</sup>

Q.65.ans: The members of the invisible church by Christ enjoy union and communion with him in grace and glory.<sup>q</sup>

Q.66.ans: The union which the elect have with Christ is the work of God’s grace,<sup>r</sup> whereby they are spiritually and mystically, yet really and inseparably, joined to Christ as their head and husband;<sup>s</sup> which is done in their effectual calling.<sup>t</sup>

Q.67.ans: Effectual calling is the work of God’s almighty power and grace,<sup>u</sup> whereby (out of his free and special love to his elect, and from nothing in them moving him thereunto<sup>w</sup> ) he doth, in his accepted time, invite and draw them to Jesus Christ, by his Word and Spirit;<sup>x</sup> savingly enlightening their minds,<sup>y</sup> renewing and powerfully deter- mining their wills,<sup>z</sup> so as they (although in themselves dead in sin) are hereby made willing and able freely to answer his call, and to accept and embrace the grace offered and conveyed therein.<sup>a</sup>

Q.68.ans: All the elect, and they only, are effectually called;<sup>b</sup> although others may be, and often are, outwardly called by the ministry of the Word,<sup>c</sup> and have some common operations of the Spirit;<sup>d</sup> who, for their willful neglect and contempt of the grace offered to them, be- ing justly left in their unbelief, do never truly come to Jesus Christ.<sup>e</sup>

Q.69.ans: The communion in grace which the members of the invisible church have with Christ, is their partaking of the virtue of his media- tion, in their justification,<sup>f</sup> adoption,<sup>g</sup> sanctification, and whatever else, in this life, manifests their union with him.<sup>h</sup>

Q.70.ans: Justification is an act of God’s free grace unto sinners,<sup>i</sup> in which he pardoneth all their sins, accepteth and accounteth their persons righteous in his sight;<sup>k</sup> not for anything wrought in them, or done by them,<sup>l</sup> but only for the perfect obedience and full satisfaction of Christ, by God imputed to them,<sup>m</sup> and received by faith alone.<sup>n</sup>

Q.71.ans: Although Christ, by his obedience and death, did make a proper, real, and full satisfaction to God’s justice in the behalf of them that are justified;<sup>o</sup> yet inasmuch as God accepteth the satisfac- tion from a surety, which he might have demanded of them, and did provide this surety, his own only Son,<sup>p</sup> imputing his righteousness to them,<sup>q</sup> and requiring nothing of them for their justification but faith,<sup>r</sup> which also is his gift,<sup>s</sup> their justification is to them of free grace.<sup>t</sup>

Q.72.ans: Justifying faith is a saving grace,<sup>u</sup> wrought in the heart of a sinner by the Spirit<sup>w</sup> and Word of God,<sup>x</sup> whereby he, being con- vinced of his sin and misery, and of the disability in himself and all other creatures to recover him out of his lost condition,<sup>y</sup> not only assenteth to the truth of the promise of the gospel,<sup>z</sup> but receiveth and resteth upon Christ and his righteousness, therein held forth, for pardon of sin,<sup>a</sup> and for the accepting and accounting of his person righteous in the sight of God for salvation.<sup>b</sup>
groups: Acts 2:37, Acts 16:30, John 16:8–9, Rom 6:6, Eph 2:1, Acts 4:12

Q.73.ans: Faith justifies a sinner in the sight of God, not because of those other graces which do always accompany it, or of good works that are the fruits of it,<sup>c</sup> nor as if the grace of faith, or any act thereof, were imputed to him for his justification;<sup>d</sup> but only as it is an instru- ment by which he receiveth and applieth Christ and his righteousness.<sup>e</sup>

Q.74.ans: Adoption is an act of the free grace of God,<sup>f</sup> in and for his only Son Jesus Christ,<sup>g</sup> whereby all those that are justified are re- ceived into the number of his children,<sup>h</sup> have his name put upon them,<sup>i</sup> the Spirit of his Son given to them,<sup>k</sup> are under his fatherly care and dispensations,<sup>l</sup> admitted to all the liberties and privileges of the sons of God, made heirs of all the promises, and fellow heirs with Christ in glory.<sup>m</sup>

Q.75.ans: Sanctification is a work of God’s grace, whereby they whom God hath, before the foundation of the world, chosen to be holy, are in time, through the powerful operation of his Spirit<sup>n</sup> applying the death and resurrection of Christ unto them,<sup>o</sup> renewed in their whole man after the image of God;<sup>p</sup> having the seeds of repentance unto life, and all other saving graces, put into their hearts,<sup>q</sup> and those graces so stirred up, increased, and strengthened,<sup>r</sup> as that they more and more die unto sin, and rise unto newness of life.<sup>s</sup>

Q.76.ans: Repentance unto life is a saving grace,<sup>t</sup> wrought in the heart of a sinner by the Spirit<sup>u</sup> and Word of God,<sup>w</sup> whereby, out of the sight and sense, not only of the danger,<sup>x</sup> but also of the filthiness and odiousness of his sins,<sup>y</sup> and upon the apprehension of God’s mercy in Christ to such as are penitent,<sup>z</sup> he so grieves for<sup>a</sup> and hates his sins,<sup>b</sup> as that he turns from them all to God,<sup>c</sup> purposing and endeavoring constantly to walk with him in all the ways of new obedience.<sup>d</sup>

Q.77.ans: Although sanctification be inseparably joined with justi- fication,<sup>e</sup> yet they differ, in that God in justification imputeth the righ- teousness of Christ;<sup>f</sup> in sanctification his Spirit infuseth grace, and enableth to the exercise thereof;<sup>g</sup> in the former, sin is pardoned;<sup>h</sup> in the other, it is subdued:<sup>i</sup> the one doth equally free all believers from the revenging wrath of God, and that perfectly in this life, that they never fall into condemnation;<sup>k</sup> the other is neither equal in all,<sup>l</sup> nor in this life perfect in any,<sup>m</sup> but growing up to perfection.<sup>n</sup>

Q.78.ans: The imperfection of sanctification in believers ariseth from the remnants of sin abiding in every part of them, and the perpetual lustings of the flesh against the spirit; whereby they are often foiled with temptations, and fall into many sins,<sup>o</sup> are hindered in all their spiritual services,<sup>p</sup> and their best works are imperfect and defiled in the sight of God.<sup>q</sup>

Q.79.ans: True believers, by reason of the unchangeable love of God,<sup>r</sup> and his decree and covenant to give them perseverance,<sup>s</sup> their in- separable union with Christ,<sup>t</sup> his continual intercession for them,<sup>u</sup> and the Spirit and seed of God abiding in them,<sup>w</sup> can neither totally nor finally fall away from the state of grace,<sup>x</sup> but are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation.<sup>y</sup>

Q.80.ans: Such as truly believe in Christ, and endeavor to walk in all good conscience before him,<sup>z</sup> may, without extraordinary revelation, by faith grounded upon the truth of God’s promises, and by the Spirit enabling them to discern in themselves those graces to which the promises of life are made,<sup>a</sup> and bearing witness with their spirits that they are the children of God,<sup>b</sup> be infallibly assured that they are in the estate of grace, and shall persevere therein unto salvation.<sup>c</sup>

Q.81.ans: Assurance of grace and salvation not being of the essence of faith,<sup>d</sup> true believers may wait long before they obtain it;<sup>e</sup> and, after the enjoyment thereof, may have it weakened and intermitted, through manifold distempers, sins, temptations, and desertions;<sup>f</sup> yet are they never left without such a presence and support of the Spirit of God as keeps them from sinking into utter despair.<sup>g</sup>

Q.82.ans: The communion in glory which the members of the invisible church have with Christ, is in this life,<sup>h</sup> immediately after death,<sup>i</sup> and at last perfected at the resurrection and day of judgment.<sup>k</sup>

Q.83.ans: The members of the invisible church have communicated to them in this life the firstfruits of glory with Christ, as they are mem- bers of him their head, and so in him are interested in that glory which he is fully possessed of;<sup>l</sup> and, as an earnest thereof, enjoy the sense of God’s love,<sup>m</sup> peace of conscience, joy in the Holy Ghost, and hope of glory;<sup>n</sup> as, on the contrary, sense of God’s revenging wrath, horror of conscience, and a fearful expectation of judgment, are to the wicked the beginning of their torments which they shall endure after death.<sup>o</sup>

Q.84.ans: Death being threatened as the wages of sin,<sup>p</sup> it is appointed unto all men once to die;<sup>q</sup> for that all have sinned.<sup>r</sup>

Q.85.ans: The righteous shall be delivered from death itself at the last day, and even in death are delivered from the sting and curse of it;<sup>s</sup> so that, although they die, yet it is out of God’s love,<sup>t</sup> to free them per- fectly from sin and misery,<sup>u</sup> and to make them capable of further communion with Christ in glory, which they then enter upon.<sup>w</sup>

Q.86.ans: The communion in glory with Christ, which the members of the invisible church enjoy immediately after death, is, in that their souls are then made perfect in holiness,<sup>x</sup> and received into the highest heavens,<sup>y</sup> where they behold the face of God in light and glory,<sup>z</sup> waiting for the full redemption of their bodies,<sup>a</sup> which even in death continue united to Christ,<sup>b</sup> and rest in their graves as in their beds,<sup>c</sup> till at the last day they be again united to their souls.<sup>d</sup> Whereas the souls of the wicked are at their death cast into hell, where they remain in torments and utter darkness, and their bodies kept in their graves, as in their prisons, till the resurrection and judgment of the great day.<sup>e</sup>

Q.87.ans: We are to believe, that at the last day there shall be a general resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust:<sup>f</sup> when they that are then found alive shall in a moment be changed; and the selfsame bodies of the dead which were laid in the grave, being then again united to their souls forever, shall be raised up by the power of Christ.<sup>g</sup> The bodies of the just, by the Spirit of Christ, and by virtue of his resurrection as their head, shall be raised in power, spiritual, incor- ruptible, and made like to his glorious body;<sup>h</sup> and the bodies of the wicked shall be raised up in dishonor by him, as an offended judge.<sup>i</sup>

Q.88.ans: Immediately after the resurrection shall follow the general and final judgment of angels and men;<sup>k</sup> the day and hour whereof no man knoweth, that all may watch and pray, and be ever ready for the coming of the Lord.<sup>l</sup>

Q.89.ans: At the day of judgment, the wicked shall be set on Christ’s left hand,<sup>m</sup> and, upon clear evidence, and full conviction of their own consciences,<sup>n</sup> shall have the fearful but just sentence of condemna- tion pronounced against them;<sup>o</sup> and thereupon shall be cast out from the favorable presence of God, and the glorious fellowship with Christ, his saints, and all his holy angels, into hell, to be punished with un- speakable torments, both of body and soul, with the devil and his angels forever.<sup>p</sup>

Q.90.ans: At the day of judgment, the righteous, being caught up to Christ in the clouds,<sup>q</sup> shall be set on his right hand, and there openly acknowledged and acquitted,<sup>r</sup> shall join with him in the judging of reprobate angels and men,<sup>s</sup> and shall be received into heaven,<sup>t</sup> where they shall be fully and forever freed from all sin and misery;<sup>u</sup> filled with inconceivable joys,<sup>w</sup> made perfectly holy and happy both in body and soul, in the company of innumerable saints and holy angels,<sup>x</sup> but especially in the immediate vision and fruition of God the Father, of our Lord Jesus Christ, and of the Holy Spirit, to all eternity.<sup>y</sup> And this is the perfect and full communion, which the members of the invisible church shall enjoy with Christ in glory, at the resurrection and day of judgment. B G , I F C

Q.91.ans: The duty which God requireth of man, is obedience to his revealed will.<sup>z</sup>

Q.92.ans: The rule of obedience revealed to Adam in the estate of inno- cence, and to all mankind in him, besides a special command not to eat of the fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, was the moral law.<sup>a</sup>

Q.93.ans: The moral law is the declaration of the will of God to man- kind, directing and binding everyone to personal, perfect, and per- petual conformity and obedience thereunto, in the frame and dispo- sition of the whole man, soul and body,<sup>b</sup> and in performance of all those duties of holiness and righteousness which he oweth to God and man:<sup>c</sup> promising life upon the fulfilling, and threatening death upon the breach of it.<sup>d</sup>

Q.94.ans: Although no man, since the fall, can attain to righteous- ness and life by the moral law;<sup>e</sup> yet there is great use thereof, as well common to all men, as peculiar either to the unregenerate, or the regenerate.<sup>f</sup>

Q.95.ans: The moral law is of use to all men, to inform them of the holy nature and will of God,<sup>g</sup> and of their duty, binding them to walk accordingly;<sup>h</sup> to convince them of their disability to keep it, and of the sinful pollution of their nature, hearts, and lives;<sup>i</sup> to humble them in the sense of their sin and misery,<sup>k</sup> and thereby help them to a clearer sight of the need they have of Christ,<sup>l</sup> and of the perfection of his obedience.<sup>m</sup>

Q.96.ans: The moral law is of use to unregenerate men, to awaken their consciences to flee from wrath to come,<sup>n</sup> and to drive them to Christ;<sup>o</sup> or, upon their continuance in the estate and way of sin, to leave them inexcusable,<sup>p</sup> and under the curse thereof.<sup>q</sup>

Q.97.ans: Although they that are regenerate, and believe in Christ, be delivered from the moral law as a covenant of works,<sup>r</sup> so as thereby they are neither justified<sup>s</sup> nor condemned;<sup>t</sup> yet, besides the general uses thereof common to them with all men, it is of special use, to show them how much they are bound to Christ for his fulfilling it, and enduring the curse thereof in their stead, and for their good;<sup>u</sup> and thereby to provoke them to more thankfulness,<sup>w</sup> and to express the same in their greater care to conform themselves thereunto as the rule of their obedience.<sup>x</sup>

Q.98.ans: The moral law is summarily comprehended in the Ten Com- mandments, which were delivered by the voice of God upon Mount Sinai, and written by him in two tables of stone;<sup>y</sup> and are recorded in the twentieth chapter of Exodus: the four first commandments con- taining our duty to God, and the other six our duty to man.<sup>z</sup>

Q.99.ans: For the right understanding of the Ten Commandments, these rules are to be observed: 1. That the law is perfect, and bindeth everyone to full confor- mity in the whole man unto the righteousness thereof, and unto entire obedience forever; so as to require the utmost per- fection of every duty, and to forbid the least degree of every sin.<sup>a</sup> 2. That it is spiritual, and so reacheth the understanding, will, affections, and all other powers of the soul; as well as words, works, and gestures.<sup>b</sup> 3. That one and the same thing, in divers respects, is required or forbidden in several commandments.<sup>c</sup> 4. That as, where a duty is commanded, the contrary sin is forbidden;<sup>d</sup> and, where a sin is forbidden, the contrary duty is commanded:<sup>e</sup> so, where a promise is annexed, the contrary threatening is included;<sup>f</sup> and, where a threatening is annexed, the contrary promise is included.<sup>g</sup> 5. That what God forbids, is at no time to be done;<sup>h</sup> what he commands, is always our duty;<sup>i</sup> and yet every particular duty is not to be done at all times.<sup>k</sup> 6. That under one sin or duty, all of the same kind are forbidden or commanded; together with all the causes, means, occasions, and appearances thereof, and provocations thereunto.<sup>l</sup> 7. That what is forbidden or commanded to ourselves, we are bound, according to our places, to endeavor that it may be avoided or performed by others, according to the duty of their places.<sup>m</sup> 8. That in what is commanded to others, we are bound, accord- ing to our places and callings, to be helpful to them;<sup>n</sup> and to take heed of partaking with others in what is forbidden them.<sup>o</sup>

Q.100.ans: We are to consider, in the Ten Commandments, the preface, the substance of the commandments themselves, and several reasons annexed to some of them, the more to enforce them.<sup>p</sup>

Q.101.ans: The preface to the Ten Commandments is contained in these words, I am the L thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.<sup>q</sup> Wherein God manifesteth his sover- eignty, as being JEHOVAH, the eternal, immutable, and almighty God;<sup>r</sup> having his being in and of himself,<sup>s</sup> and giving being to all his words<sup>t</sup> and works:<sup>u</sup> and that he is a God in covenant, as with Israel of old, so with all his people;<sup>w</sup> who, as he brought them out of their bondage in Egypt, so he delivereth us from our spiritual thraldom;<sup>x</sup> and that therefore we are bound to take him for our God alone, and to keep all his commandments.<sup>y</sup>

Q.102.ans: The sum of the four commandments containing our duty to God is, to love the Lord our God with all our heart, and with all our soul, and with all our strength, and with all our mind.<sup>z</sup>

Q.103.ans: The first commandment is, Thou shall have no other gods before me.<sup>a</sup>

Q.104.ans: The duties required in the first commandment are, the knowing and acknowledging of God to be the only true God, and our God;<sup>b</sup> and to worship and glorify him accordingly,<sup>c</sup> by think- ing,<sup>d</sup> meditating,<sup>e</sup> remembering,<sup>f</sup> highly esteeming,<sup>g</sup> honoring,<sup>h</sup> adoring,<sup>i</sup> choosing,<sup>k</sup> loving,<sup>l</sup> desiring,<sup>m</sup> fearing of him;<sup>n</sup> believing him;<sup>o</sup> trusting,<sup>p</sup> hoping,<sup>q</sup> delighting,<sup>r</sup> rejoicing in him;<sup>s</sup> being zealous for him;<sup>t</sup> calling upon him, giving all praise and thanks,<sup>u</sup> and yielding all obedience and submission to him with the whole man;<sup>w</sup> being careful in all things to please him,<sup>x</sup> and sorrowful when in anything he is offended;<sup>y</sup> and walking humbly with him.<sup>z</sup>

Q.105.ans: The sins forbidden in the first commandment are, atheism, in denying or not having a God;<sup>a</sup> idolatry, in having or worshiping more gods than one, or any with or instead of the true God;<sup>b</sup> the not hav- ing and avouching him for God, and our God;<sup>c</sup> the omission or ne- glect of anything due to him, required in this commandment;<sup>d</sup> igno- rance,<sup>e</sup> forgetfulness,<sup>f</sup> misapprehensions,<sup>g</sup> false opinions,<sup>h</sup> unworthy and wicked thoughts of him;<sup>i</sup> bold and curious searching into his secrets;<sup>k</sup> all profaneness,<sup>l</sup> hatred of God;<sup>m</sup> self-love,<sup>n</sup> self-seeking,<sup>o</sup> and all other inordinate and immoderate setting of our mind, will, or affections upon other things, and taking them off from him in whole or in part;<sup>p</sup> vain credulity,<sup>q</sup> unbelief,<sup>r</sup> heresy,<sup>s</sup> misbelief,<sup>t</sup> distrust,<sup>u</sup> despair,<sup>w</sup> incorrigibleness,<sup>x</sup> and insensibleness under judgments,<sup>y</sup> hardness of heart,<sup>z</sup> pride,<sup>a´</sup> presumption,<sup>b´</sup> carnal security,<sup>c´</sup> tempt- ing of God;<sup>d´</sup> using unlawful means,<sup>e´</sup> and trusting in lawful means;<sup>f´</sup> carnal delights and joys;<sup>g´</sup> corrupt, blind, and indiscreet zeal;<sup>h´</sup> luke- warmness,<sup>i´</sup> and deadness in the things of God;<sup>k´</sup> estranging ourselves, and apostatizing from God;<sup>l´</sup> praying, or giving any religious wor- ship, to saints, angels, or any other creatures;<sup>m´</sup> all compacts and consulting with the devil,<sup>n´</sup> and hearkening to his suggestions;<sup>o´</sup> mak- ing men the lords of our faith and conscience;<sup>p´</sup> slighting and despis- ing God and his commands;<sup>q´</sup> resisting and grieving of his Spirit,<sup>r´</sup> discontent and impatience at his dispensations, charging him fool- ishly for the evils he inflicts on us;<sup>s´</sup> and ascribing the praise of any good we either are, have, or can do, to fortune,<sup>t´</sup> idols,<sup>u´</sup> ourselves,<sup>w´</sup> or any other creature.<sup>x´</sup>

Q.106.ans: These words before me or before my face, in the first command- ment, teach us, that God, who seeth all things, taketh special notice of, and is much displeased with, the sin of having any other God: that so it may be an argument to dissuade from it, and to aggravate it as a most impudent provocation:<sup>y</sup> as also to persuade us to do as in his sight, whatever we do in his service.<sup>z</sup>

Q.107.ans: The second commandment is, Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth: thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the L thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me; and shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments.<sup>a</sup>

Q.108.ans: The duties required in the second commandment are, the re- ceiving, observing, and keeping pure and entire, all such religious worship and ordinances as God hath instituted in his Word;<sup>b</sup> particu- larly prayer and thanksgiving in the name of Christ;<sup>c</sup> the reading, preaching, and hearing of the Word;<sup>d</sup> the administration and re- ceiving of the sacraments;<sup>e</sup> church government and discipline;<sup>f</sup> the ministry and maintainance thereof;<sup>g</sup> religious fasting;<sup>h</sup> swearing by the name of God,<sup>i</sup> and vowing unto him:<sup>k</sup> as also the disapproving, detesting, opposing all false worship;<sup>l</sup> and, according to each one’s place and calling, removing it, and all monuments of idolatry.<sup>m</sup>

Q.109.ans: The sins forbidden in the second commandment are, all de- vising,<sup>n</sup> counseling,<sup>o</sup> commanding,<sup>p</sup> using,<sup>q</sup> and anywise approving, any religious worship not instituted by God himself;<sup>r</sup> the making any representation of God, of all or of any of the three persons, either inwardly in our mind, or outwardly in any kind of image or likeness of any creature whatsoever;<sup>s</sup> all worshiping of it,<sup>t</sup> or God in it or by it;<sup>u</sup> the making of any representation of feigned deities,<sup>w</sup> and all wor- ship of them, or service belonging to them;<sup>x</sup> all superstitious devices,<sup>y</sup> corrupting the worship of God,<sup>z</sup> adding to it, or taking from it,<sup>a</sup> whether invented and taken up of ourselves,<sup>b</sup> or received by tradi- tion from others,<sup>c</sup> though under the title of antiquity,<sup>d</sup> custom,<sup>e</sup> devotion,<sup>f</sup> good intent, or any other pretense whatsoever;<sup>g</sup> simony;<sup>h</sup> sacrilege;<sup>i</sup> all neglect,<sup>k</sup> contempt,<sup>l</sup> hindering,<sup>m</sup> and opposing the wor- ship and ordinances which God hath appointed.<sup>n´</sup>

Q.110.ans: The reasons annexed to the second commandment, the more to enforce it, contained in these words, For I the L thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me; and shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments;<sup>o</sup> are, besides God’s sover- eignty over us, and propriety in us,<sup>p</sup> his fervent zeal for his own worship,<sup>q</sup> and his revengeful indignation against all false worship, as being a spiritual whoredom;<sup>r</sup> accounting the breakers of this com- mandment such as hate him, and threatening to punish them unto divers generations;<sup>s</sup> and esteeming the observers of it such as love him and keep his commandments, and promising mercy to them unto many generations.<sup>t</sup>

Q.111.ans: The third commandment is, Thou shalt not take the name of the L thy God in vain; for the L will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.<sup>u</sup>

Q.112.ans: The third commandment requires, that the name of God, his titles, attributes,<sup>w</sup> ordinances,<sup>x</sup> the Word,<sup>y</sup> sacraments,<sup>z</sup> prayer,<sup>a</sup> oaths,<sup>b</sup> vows,<sup>c</sup> lots,<sup>d</sup> his works,<sup>e</sup> and whatsoever else there is whereby he makes himself known, be holily and reverently used in thought,<sup>f</sup> meditation,<sup>g</sup> word,<sup>h</sup> and writing;<sup>i</sup> by an holy profession,<sup>k</sup> and answerable conversation,<sup>l</sup> to the glory of God,<sup>m</sup> and the good of ourselves,<sup>n</sup> and others.<sup>o</sup>

Q.113.ans: The sins forbidden in the third commandment are, the not using of God’s name as is required;<sup>p</sup> and the abuse of it in an ignorant,<sup>q</sup> vain,<sup>r</sup> irreverent, profane,<sup>s</sup> superstitious,<sup>t</sup> or wicked men- tioning or otherwise using his titles, attributes,<sup>u</sup> ordinances,<sup>w</sup> or works,<sup>x</sup> by blasphemy,<sup>y</sup> perjury;<sup>z</sup> all sinful cursings,<sup>a</sup> oaths,<sup>b</sup> vows,<sup>c</sup> and lots;<sup>d</sup> violating of our oaths and vows, if lawful,<sup>e</sup> and fulfilling them, if of things unlawful;<sup>f</sup> murmuring and quarreling at,<sup>g</sup> curious prying into,<sup>h</sup> and misapplying of God’s decrees<sup>i</sup> and providences;<sup>k</sup> misinterpreting,<sup>l</sup> misapplying,<sup>m</sup> or anyway perverting the Word, or any part of it,<sup>n</sup> to profane jests,<sup>o</sup> curious or unprofitable questions, vain janglings, or the maintaining of false doctrines;<sup>p´</sup> abusing it, the creatures, or any- thing contained under the name of God, to charms,<sup>q´</sup> or sinful lusts and practices;<sup>r´</sup> the maligning,<sup>s´</sup> scorning,<sup>t´</sup> reviling,<sup>u´</sup> or anywise op- posing of God’s truth, grace, and ways;<sup>w´</sup> making profession of reli- gion in hypocrisy, or for sinister ends;<sup>x´</sup> being ashamed of it,<sup>y´</sup> or a shame to it, by unconformable,<sup>z´</sup> unwise,<sup>a´</sup> unfruitful,<sup>b´</sup> and offensive walking,<sup>c´</sup> or backsliding from it.<sup>d´</sup>

Q.114.ans: The reasons annexed to the third commandment, in these words, The L thy God, and, For the L will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain,<sup>e</sup> are, because he is the Lord and our God, there- fore his name is not to be profaned, or anyway abused by us;<sup>f</sup> espe- cially because he will be so far from acquitting and sparing the trans- gressors of this commandment, as that he will not suffer them to escape his righteous judgment,<sup>g</sup> albeit many such escape the cen- sures and punishments of men.<sup>h</sup>

Q.115.ans: The fourth commandment is, Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work: but the seventh day is the sabbath of the L thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates: for in six days the L made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that in them is, and rested the seventh day: wherefore the L blessed the sabbath day and hallowed it.<sup>i</sup>

Q.116.ans: The fourth commandment requireth of all men the sanctify- ing or keeping holy to God such set times as he hath appointed in his Word, expressly one whole day in seven; which was the seventh from the beginning of the world to the resurrection of Christ, and the first day of the week ever since, and so to continue to the end of the world; which is the Christian sabbath,<sup>k</sup> and in the New Testament called the Lord’s Day.<sup>l</sup>

Q.117.ans: The Sabbath or Lord’s Day is to be sanctified by an holy rest- ing all the day,<sup>m</sup> not only from such works as are at all times sinful, but even from such worldly employments and recreations as are on other days lawful;<sup>n</sup> and making it our delight to spend the whole time (except so much of it as is to be taken up in works of necessity and mercy<sup>o</sup> ) in the public and private exercises of God’s worship:<sup>p</sup> and, to that end, we are to prepare our hearts, and with such foresight, dili- gence, and moderation, to dispose and seasonably dispatch our worldly business, that we may be the more free and fit for the duties of that day.<sup>q</sup>

Q.118.ans: The charge of keeping the Sabbath is more specially directed to governors of families, and other superiors, because they are bound not only to keep it themselves, but to see that it be observed by all those that are under their charge; and because they are prone ofttimes to hinder them by employments of their own.<sup>r</sup>

Q.119.ans: The sins forbidden in the fourth commandment are, all omis- sions of the duties required,<sup>s</sup> all careless, negligent, and unprofitable performing of them, and being weary of them;<sup>t</sup> all profaning the day by idleness, and doing that which is in itself sinful;<sup>u</sup> and by all need- less works, words, and thoughts, about our worldly employments and recreations.<sup>w</sup>

Q.120.ans: The reasons annexed to the fourth commandment, the more to enforce it, are taken from the equity of it, God allowing us six days of seven for our own affairs, and reserving but one for himself, in these words, Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work:<sup>x</sup> from God’s challenging a special propriety in that day, The seventh day is the sabbath of the L thy God:<sup>y</sup> from the example of God, who in six days … made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that in them is, and rested the seventh day: and from that blessing which God put upon that day, not only in sanctify- ing it to be a day for his service, but in ordaining it to be a means of blessing to us in our sanctifying it; Wherefore the L blessed the sabbath day, and hallowed it.<sup>z</sup>

Q.121.ans: The word Remember is set in the beginning of the fourth commandment,<sup>a</sup> partly, because of the great benefit of remember- ing it, we being thereby helped in our preparation to keep it,<sup>b</sup> and, in keeping it, better to keep all the rest of the commandments,<sup>c</sup> and to continue a thankful remembrance of the two great benefits of cre- ation and redemption, which contain a short abridgment of religion;<sup>d</sup> and partly, because we are very ready to forget it,<sup>e</sup> for that there is less light of nature for it,<sup>f</sup> and yet it restraineth our natural liberty in things at other times lawful;<sup>g</sup> that it cometh but once in seven days, and many worldly businesses come between, and too often take off our minds from thinking of it, either to prepare for it, or to sanctify it;<sup>h</sup> and that Satan with his instruments much labor to blot out the glory, and even the memory of it, to bring in all irreligion and impiety.<sup>i</sup>

Q.122.ans: The sum of the six commandments which contain our duty to man is, to love our neighbor as ourselves,<sup>k</sup> and to do to others what we would have them to do to us.<sup>l</sup>

Q.123.ans: The fifth commandment is, Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which the L thy God giveth thee.<sup>m</sup>

Q.124.ans: By father and mother, in the fifth commandment, are meant, not only natural parents,<sup>n</sup> but all superiors in age<sup>o</sup> and gifts;<sup>p</sup> and espe- cially such as, by God’s ordinance, are over us in place of authority, whether in family,<sup>q</sup> church,<sup>r</sup> or commonwealth.<sup>s</sup>

Q.125.ans: Superiors are styled father and mother, both to teach them in all duties toward their inferiors, like natural parents, to express love and tenderness to them, according to their several relations;<sup>t</sup> and to work inferiors to a greater willingness and cheerfulness in performing their duties to their superiors, as to their parents.<sup>u</sup>

Q.126.ans: The general scope of the fifth commandment is, the perfor- mance of those duties which we mutually owe in our several rela- tions, as inferiors, superiors, or equals.<sup>w</sup>

Q.127.ans: The honor which inferiors owe to their superiors is, all due reverence in heart,<sup>x</sup> word,<sup>y</sup> and behavior;<sup>z</sup> prayer and thanksgiving for them;<sup>a</sup> imitation of their virtues and graces;<sup>b</sup> willing obedience to their lawful commands and counsels;<sup>c</sup> due submission to their corrections;<sup>d</sup> fidelity to,<sup>e</sup> defense,<sup>f</sup> and maintenance of their persons and authority, according to their several ranks, and the nature of their places;<sup>g</sup> bearing with their infirmities, and covering them in love,<sup>h</sup> that so they may be an honor to them and to their government.<sup>i</sup>

Q.128.ans: The sins of inferiors against their superiors are, all neglect of the duties required toward them;<sup>k</sup> envying at,<sup>l</sup> contempt of,<sup>m</sup> and rebellion<sup>n</sup> against, their persons<sup>o</sup> and places,<sup>p</sup> in their lawful counsels,<sup>q</sup> commands, and corrections;<sup>r</sup> cursing, mocking,<sup>s</sup> and all such refrac- tory and scandalous carriage, as proves a shame and dishonor to them and their government.<sup>t</sup>

Q.129.ans: It is required of superiors, according to that power they re- ceive from God, and that relation wherein they stand, to love,<sup>u</sup> pray for,<sup>w</sup> and bless their inferiors;<sup>x</sup> to instruct,<sup>y</sup> counsel, and admonish them;<sup>z</sup> countenancing,<sup>a</sup> commending,<sup>b</sup> and rewarding such as do well;<sup>c</sup> and discountenancing,<sup>d</sup> reproving, and chastising such as do ill;<sup>e</sup> protecting,<sup>f</sup> and providing for them all things necessary for soul<sup>g</sup> and body:<sup>h</sup> and by grave, wise, holy, and exemplary carriage, to procure glory to God,<sup>i</sup> honor to themselves,<sup>k</sup> and so to preserve that authority which God hath put upon them.<sup>l</sup>

Q.130.ans: The sins of superiors are, besides the neglect of the duties required of them,<sup>m</sup> and inordinate seeking of themselves,<sup>n</sup> their own glory,<sup>o</sup> ease, profit, or pleasure;<sup>p</sup> commanding things unlawful,<sup>q</sup> or not in the power of inferiors to perform;<sup>r</sup> counseling,<sup>s</sup> encouraging,<sup>t</sup> or favoring them in that which is evil;<sup>u</sup> dissuading, discouraging, or discountenancing them in that which is good;<sup>w</sup> correcting them unduly;<sup>x</sup> careless exposing, or leaving them to wrong, temptation, and danger;<sup>y</sup> provoking them to wrath;<sup>z</sup> or anyway dishonoring them- selves, or lessening their authority, by an unjust, indiscreet, rigorous, or remiss behavior.<sup>a</sup>

Q.131.ans: The duties of equals are, to regard the dignity and worth of each other,<sup>b</sup> in giving honor to go one before another;<sup>c</sup> and to rejoice in each other’s gifts and advancement, as their own.<sup>d</sup>

Q.132.ans: The sins of equals are, besides the neglect of the duties required,<sup>e</sup> the undervaluing of the worth,<sup>f</sup> envying the gifts,<sup>g</sup> griev- ing at the advancement of prosperity one of another;<sup>h</sup> and usurping preeminence one over another.<sup>i</sup>

Q.133.ans: The reason annexed to the fifth commandment, in these words, That thy days may be long upon the land which the L thy God giveth thee,<sup>k</sup> is an express promise of long life and prosperity, as far as it shall serve for God’s glory and their own good, to all such as keep this commandment.<sup>l</sup>

Q.134.ans: The sixth commandment is, Thou shalt not kill.<sup>m</sup>

Q.135.ans: The duties required in the sixth commandment are, all care- ful studies, and lawful endeavors, to preserve the life of ourselves<sup>n</sup> and others<sup>o</sup> by resisting all thoughts and purposes,<sup>p</sup> subduing all passions,<sup>q</sup> and avoiding all occasions,<sup>r</sup> temptations,<sup>s</sup> and practices, which tend to the unjust taking away the life of any;<sup>t</sup> by just defense thereof against violence,<sup>u</sup> patient bearing of the hand of God,<sup>w</sup> quiet- ness of mind,<sup>x</sup> cheerfulness of spirit;<sup>y</sup> a sober use of meat,<sup>z</sup> drink,<sup>a</sup> physic,<sup>b</sup> sleep,<sup>c</sup> labor,<sup>d</sup> and recreations;<sup>e</sup> by charitable thoughts,<sup>f</sup> love,<sup>g</sup> compassion,<sup>h</sup> meekness, gentleness, kindness;<sup>i</sup> peaceable,<sup>k</sup> mild, and courteous speeches and behavior;<sup>l</sup> forbearance, readiness to be reconciled, patient bearing and forgiving of injuries, and requiting good for evil;<sup>m</sup> comforting and succoring the distressed, and protect- ing and defending the innocent.<sup>n´</sup>

Q.136.ans: The sins forbidden in the sixth commandment are, all taking away the life of ourselves,<sup>o</sup> or of others,<sup>p</sup> except in case of public justice,<sup>q</sup> lawful war,<sup>r</sup> or necessary defense;<sup>s</sup> the neglecting or with- drawing the lawful and necessary means of preservation of life;<sup>t</sup> sin- ful anger,<sup>u</sup> hatred,<sup>w</sup> envy,<sup>x</sup> desire of revenge;<sup>y</sup> all excessive passions,<sup>z</sup> distracting cares;<sup>a</sup> immoderate use of meat, drink,<sup>b</sup> labor,<sup>c</sup> and recreations;<sup>d</sup> provoking words,<sup>e</sup> oppression,<sup>f</sup> quarreling,<sup>g</sup> striking, wounding,<sup>h</sup> and whatsoever else tends to the destruction of the life of any.<sup>i</sup>

Q.137.ans: The seventh commandment is, Thou shalt not commit adultery.<sup>k</sup>

Q.138.ans: The duties required in the seventh commandment are, chas- tity in body, mind, affections,<sup>l</sup> words,<sup>m</sup> and behavior;<sup>n</sup> and the preser- vation of it in ourselves and others;<sup>o</sup> watchfulness over the eyes and all the senses;<sup>p</sup> temperance,<sup>q</sup> keeping of chaste company,<sup>r</sup> modesty in apparel;<sup>s</sup> marriage by those that have not the gift of continency,<sup>t</sup> conjugal love,<sup>u</sup> and cohabitation;<sup>w</sup> diligent labor in our callings;<sup>x</sup> shun- ning all occasions of uncleanness, and resisting temptations thereunto.<sup>y</sup>

Q.139.ans: The sins forbidden in the seventh commandment, besides the neglect of the duties required,<sup>z</sup> are, adultery, fornication,<sup>a</sup> rape, incest,<sup>b</sup> sodomy, and all unnatural lusts;<sup>c</sup> all unclean imaginations, thoughts, purposes, and affections;<sup>d</sup> all corrupt or filthy communications, or listening thereunto;<sup>e</sup> wanton looks,<sup>f</sup> impudent or light behavior, im- modest apparel;<sup>g</sup> prohibiting of lawful,<sup>h</sup> and dispensing with unlaw- ful marriages;<sup>i</sup> allowing, tolerating, keeping of stews, and resorting to them;<sup>k</sup> entangling vows of single life,<sup>l</sup> undue delay of marriage,<sup>m</sup> having more wives or husbands than one at the same time;<sup>n</sup> unjust divorce,<sup>o</sup> or desertion;<sup>p</sup> idleness, gluttony, drunkenness,<sup>q</sup> unchaste company;<sup>r</sup> lascivious songs, books, pictures, dancings, stage plays;<sup>s</sup> and all other provocations to, or acts of uncleanness, either in our- selves or others.<sup>t</sup>

Q.140.ans: The eighth commandment is, Thou shalt not steal.<sup>u</sup>

Q.141.ans: The duties required in the eighth commandment are, truth, faithfulness, and justice in contracts and commerce between man and man;<sup>w</sup> rendering to everyone his due;<sup>x</sup> restitution of goods unlaw- fully detained from the right owners thereof;<sup>y</sup> giving and lending freely, according to our abilities, and the necessities of others;<sup>z</sup> moderation of our judgments, wills, and affections concerning worldly goods;<sup>a</sup> a provident care and study to get,<sup>b</sup> keep, use, and dispose these things which are necessary and convenient for the sustentation of our na- ture, and suitable to our condition;<sup>c</sup> a lawful calling,<sup>d</sup> and diligence in it;<sup>e</sup> frugality;<sup>f</sup> avoiding unnecessary lawsuits,<sup>g</sup> and suretyship, or other like engagements;<sup>h</sup> and an endeavor, by all just and lawful means, to procure, preserve, and further the wealth and outward estate of oth- ers, as well as our own.<sup>i</sup>

Q.142.ans: The sins forbidden in the eighth commandment, besides the neglect of the duties required,<sup>k</sup> are, theft,<sup>l</sup> robbery,<sup>m</sup> manstealing,<sup>n</sup> and receiving anything that is stolen;<sup>o</sup> fraudulent dealing,<sup>p</sup> false weights and measures,<sup>q</sup> removing landmarks,<sup>r</sup> injustice and unfaithfulness in contracts between man and man,<sup>s</sup> or in matters of trust;<sup>t</sup> oppression,<sup>u</sup> extortion,<sup>w</sup> usury,<sup>x</sup> bribery,<sup>y</sup> vexatious lawsuits,<sup>z</sup> unjust enclosures and depredation;<sup>a</sup> engrossing commodities to enhance the price;<sup>b</sup> un- lawful callings,<sup>c</sup> and all other unjust or sinful ways of taking or with- holding from our neighbor what belongs to him, or of enriching ourselves;<sup>d</sup> covetousness;<sup>e</sup> inordinate prizing and affecting worldly goods;<sup>f</sup> distrustful and distracting cares and studies in getting, keep- ing, and using them;<sup>g</sup> envying at the prosperity of others;<sup>h</sup> as likewise idleness,<sup>i</sup> prodigality, wasteful gaming; and all other ways whereby we do unduly prejudice our own outward estate,<sup>k´</sup> and defrauding ourselves of the due use and comfort of that estate which God hath given us.<sup>l´</sup>

Q.143.ans: The ninth commandment is, Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.<sup>m</sup>

Q.144.ans: The duties required in the ninth commandment are, the pre- serving and promoting of truth between man and man,<sup>n</sup> and the good name of our neighbor, as well as our own;<sup>o</sup> appearing and stand- ing for the truth;<sup>p</sup> and from the heart,<sup>q</sup> sincerely,<sup>r</sup> freely,<sup>s</sup> clearly,<sup>t</sup> and fully,<sup>u</sup> speaking the truth, and only the truth, in matters of judgment and justice,<sup>w</sup> and in all other things whatsoever;<sup>x</sup> a charitable esteem of our neighbors;<sup>y</sup> loving, desiring, and rejoicing in their good name;<sup>z</sup> sorrowing for,<sup>a</sup> and covering of their infirmities;<sup>b</sup> freely acknowledg- ing of their gifts and graces,<sup>c</sup> defending their innocency;<sup>d</sup> a ready receiving of a good report,<sup>e</sup> and unwillingness to admit of an evil report,<sup>f</sup> concerning them; discouraging talebearers,<sup>g</sup> flatterers,<sup>h</sup> and slanderers;<sup>i</sup> love and care of our own good name, and defending it when need requireth;<sup>k</sup> keeping of lawful promises;<sup>l</sup> studying and prac- ticing of whatsoever things are true, honest, lovely, and of good report.<sup>m</sup>

Q.145.ans: The sins forbidden in the ninth commandment are, all preju- dicing the truth, and the good name of our neighbors, as well as our own,<sup>n</sup> especially in public judicature;<sup>o</sup> giving false evidence,<sup>p</sup> suborn- ing false witnesses,<sup>q</sup> wittingly appearing and pleading for an evil cause, outfacing and overbearing the truth;<sup>r</sup> passing unjust sentence,<sup>s</sup> call- ing evil good, and good evil; rewarding the wicked according to the work of the righteous, and the righteous according to the work of the wicked;<sup>t</sup> forgery,<sup>u</sup> concealing the truth, undue silence in a just cause,<sup>w</sup> and holding our peace when iniquity calleth for either a reproof from ourselves,<sup>x</sup> or complaint to others;<sup>y</sup> speaking the truth unseasonably,<sup>z</sup> or maliciously to a wrong end,<sup>a</sup> or perverting it to a wrong meaning,<sup>b</sup> or in doubtful and equivocal expressions, to the prejudice of truth or justice;<sup>c</sup> speaking untruth,<sup>d</sup> lying,<sup>e</sup> slandering,<sup>f</sup> backbiting,<sup>g</sup> detracting,<sup>h</sup> talebearing,<sup>i</sup> whispering,<sup>k</sup> scoffing,<sup>l</sup> reviling,<sup>m</sup> rash,<sup>n´</sup> harsh,<sup>o´</sup> and partial censuring;<sup>p´</sup> misconstructing intentions, words, and actions;<sup>q´</sup> flattering,<sup>r´</sup> vainglorious boasting;<sup>s´</sup> thinking or speak- ing too highly or too meanly of ourselves or others;<sup>t´</sup> denying the gifts and graces of God;<sup>u´</sup> aggravating smaller faults;<sup>w´</sup> hiding, excusing, or extenuating of sins, when called to a free confession;<sup>x´</sup> unneces- sary discovering of infirmities;<sup>y´</sup> raising false rumors,<sup>z´</sup> receiving and countenancing evil reports,<sup>a´</sup> and stopping our ears against just defense;<sup>b´</sup> evil suspicion;<sup>c´</sup> envying or grieving at the deserved credit of any,<sup>d´</sup> endeavoring or desiring to impair it,<sup>e´</sup> rejoicing in their dis- grace and infamy;<sup>f´</sup> scornful contempt,<sup>g´</sup> fond admiration;<sup>h´</sup> breach of lawful promises;<sup>i´</sup> neglecting such things as are of good report,<sup>k´</sup> and practicing, or not avoiding ourselves, or not hindering what we can in others, such things as procure an ill name.<sup>l´</sup>

Q.146.ans: The tenth commandment is, Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shall not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.<sup>m</sup>

Q.147.ans: The duties required in the tenth commandment are, such a full contentment with our own condition,<sup>n</sup> and such a charitable frame of the whole soul toward our neighbor, as that all our inward mo- tions and affections touching him, tend unto, and further all that good which is his.<sup>o</sup>

Q.148.ans: The sins forbidden in the tenth commandment are, discon- tentment with our own estate;<sup>p</sup> envying<sup>q</sup> and grieving at the good of our neighbor,<sup>r</sup> together with all inordinate motions and affections to anything that is his.<sup>s</sup>

Q.149.ans: No man is able, either of himself,<sup>t</sup> or by any grace received in this life, perfectly to keep the commandments of God;<sup>u</sup> but doth daily break them in thought,<sup>w</sup> word, and deed.<sup>x</sup>

Q.150.ans: All transgressions of the law of God are not equally heinous; but some sins in themselves, and by reason of several aggravations, are more heinous in the sight of God than others.<sup>y</sup>

Q.151.ans: Sins receive their aggravations, 1. From the persons offending:<sup>z</sup> if they be of riper age,<sup>a</sup> greater experience or grace,<sup>b</sup> eminent for profession,<sup>c</sup> gifts,<sup>d</sup> place,<sup>e</sup> office,<sup>f</sup> guides to others,<sup>g</sup> and whose example is likely to be followed by others.<sup>h</sup> 2. From the parties offended:<sup>i</sup> if immediately against God,<sup>k</sup> his attributes,<sup>l</sup> and worship;<sup>m</sup> against Christ, and his grace;<sup>n</sup> the Holy Spirit,<sup>o</sup> his witness,<sup>p</sup> and workings;<sup>q</sup> against superiors, men of eminency,<sup>r</sup> and such as we stand especially related and engaged unto;<sup>s</sup> against any of the saints,<sup>t</sup> particularly weak brethren,<sup>u</sup> the souls of them, or any other,<sup>w</sup> and the common good of all or many.<sup>x</sup> 3. From the nature and quality of the offense:<sup>y</sup> if it be against the express letter of the law,<sup>z</sup> break many commandments, contain in it many sins:<sup>a</sup> if not only conceived in the heart, but breaks forth in words and actions,<sup>b</sup> scandalize others,<sup>c</sup> and admit of no reparation:<sup>d</sup> if against means,<sup>e</sup> mercies,<sup>f</sup> judg- ments,<sup>g</sup> light of nature,<sup>h</sup> conviction of conscience,<sup>i</sup> public or private admonition,<sup>k</sup> censures of the church,<sup>l</sup> civil pun- ishments;<sup>m</sup> and our prayers, purposes, promises,<sup>n</sup> vows,<sup>o</sup> covenants,<sup>p</sup> and engagements to God or men:<sup>q</sup> if done deliberately,<sup>r</sup> willfully,<sup>s</sup> presumptuously,<sup>t</sup> impudently,<sup>u</sup> boastingly,<sup>w</sup> maliciously,<sup>x</sup> frequently,<sup>y´</sup> obstinately,<sup>z´</sup> with delight,<sup>a´</sup> continuance,<sup>b´</sup> or relapsing after repentance.<sup>c´</sup> 4. From circumstances of time<sup>d</sup> and place:<sup>e</sup> if on the Lord’s Day,<sup>f</sup> or other times of divine worship;<sup>g</sup> or immediately before<sup>h</sup> or after these,<sup>i</sup> or other helps to prevent or remedy such mis- carriages:<sup>k</sup> if in public, or in the presence of others, who are thereby likely to be provoked or defiled.<sup>l</sup>

Q.152.ans: Every sin, even the least, being against the sovereignty,<sup>m</sup> goodness,<sup>n</sup> and holiness of God,<sup>o</sup> and against his righteous law,<sup>p</sup> deserveth his wrath and curse,<sup>q</sup> both in this life,<sup>r</sup> and that which is to come;<sup>s</sup> and cannot be expiated but by the blood of Christ.<sup>t</sup>

Q.153.ans: That we may escape the wrath and curse of God due to us by reason of the transgression of the law, he requireth of us repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ,<sup>u</sup> and the dili- gent use of the outward means whereby Christ communicates to us the benefits of his mediation.<sup>w</sup>

Q.154.ans: The outward and ordinary means whereby Christ communi- cates to his church the benefits of his mediation, are all his ordi- nances; especially the Word, sacraments, and prayer; all which are made effectual to the elect for their salvation.<sup>x</sup>

Q.155.ans: The Spirit of God maketh the reading, but especially the preaching of the Word, an effectual means of enlightening,<sup>y</sup> con- vincing, and humbling sinners;<sup>z</sup> of driving them out of them- selves, and drawing them unto Christ;<sup>a</sup> of conforming them to his image,<sup>b</sup> and subduing them to his will;<sup>c</sup> of strengthening them against temptations and corruptions;<sup>d</sup> of building them up in grace,<sup>e</sup> and establishing their hearts in holiness and comfort through faith unto salvation.<sup>f</sup>

Q.156.ans: Although all are not to be permitted to read the Word pub- licly to the congregation,<sup>g</sup> yet all sorts of people are bound to read it apart by themselves,<sup>h</sup> and with their families:<sup>i</sup> to which end, the Holy Scriptures are to be translated out of the original into vulgar languages.<sup>k</sup>

Q.157.ans: The Holy Scriptures are to be read with an high and reverent esteem of them;<sup>l</sup> with a firm persuasion that they are the very Word of God,<sup>m</sup> and that he only can enable us to understand them;<sup>n</sup> with desire to know, believe, and obey the will of God revealed in them;<sup>o</sup> with diligence,<sup>p</sup> and attention to the matter and scope of them;<sup>q</sup> with meditation,<sup>r</sup> application,<sup>s</sup> self-denial,<sup>t</sup> and prayer.<sup>u</sup>

Q.158.ans: The Word of God is to be preached only by such as are suffi- ciently gifted,<sup>w</sup> and also duly approved and called to that office.<sup>x</sup>

Q.159.ans: They that are called to labor in the ministry of the Word, are to preach sound doctrine,<sup>y</sup> diligently,<sup>z</sup> in season and out of season;<sup>a</sup> plainly,<sup>b</sup> not in the enticing words of man’s wisdom, but in demon- stration of the Spirit, and of power;<sup>c</sup> faithfully,<sup>d</sup> making known the whole counsel of God;<sup>e</sup> wisely,<sup>f</sup> applying themselves to the necessi- ties and capacities of the hearers;<sup>g</sup> zealously,<sup>h</sup> with fervent love to God<sup>i</sup> and the souls of his people;<sup>k</sup> sincerely,<sup>l</sup> aiming at his glory,<sup>m</sup> and their conversion,<sup>n</sup> edification,<sup>o</sup> and salvation.<sup>p</sup>

Q.160.ans: It is required of those that hear the Word preached, that they attend upon it with diligence,<sup>q</sup> preparation,<sup>r</sup> and prayer;<sup>s</sup> examine what they hear by the Scriptures;<sup>t</sup> receive the truth with faith,<sup>u</sup> love,<sup>w</sup> meekness,<sup>x</sup> and readiness of mind,<sup>y</sup> as the Word of God;<sup>z</sup> meditate,<sup>a</sup> and confer of it;<sup>b</sup> hide it in their hearts,<sup>c</sup> and bring forth the fruit of it in their lives.<sup>d</sup>

Q.161.ans: The sacraments become effectual means of salvation, not by any power in themselves, or any virtue derived from the piety or in- tention of him by whom they are administered, but only by the work- ing of the Holy Ghost, and the blessing of Christ, by whom they are instituted.<sup>e</sup>

Q.162.ans: A sacrament is an holy ordinance instituted by Christ in his church,<sup>f</sup> to signify, seal, and exhibit<sup>g</sup> unto those that are within the covenant of grace,<sup>h</sup> the benefits of his mediation;<sup>i</sup> to strengthen and increase their faith, and all other graces;<sup>k</sup> to oblige them to obedience;<sup>l</sup> to testify and cherish their love and communion one with another;<sup>m</sup> and to distinguish them from those that are without.<sup>n</sup>

Q.163.ans: The parts of a sacrament are two; the one an outward and sensible sign, used according to Christ’s own appointment; the other an inward and spiritual grace thereby signified.<sup>o</sup>

Q.164.ans: Under the new testament Christ hath instituted in his church only two sacraments, baptism and the Lord’s Supper.<sup>p</sup>

Q.165.ans: Baptism is a sacrament of the new testament, wherein Christ hath ordained the washing with water in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost,<sup>q</sup> to be a sign and seal of ingrafting into himself,<sup>r</sup> of remission of sins by his blood,<sup>s</sup> and regeneration by his Spirit;<sup>t</sup> of adoption,<sup>u</sup> and resurrection unto everlasting life;<sup>w</sup> and whereby the parties baptized are solemnly admitted into the visible church,<sup>x</sup> and enter into an open and professed engagement to be wholly and only the Lord’s.<sup>y</sup>

Q.166.ans: Baptism is not to be administered to any that are out of the visible church, and so strangers from the covenant of promise, till they profess their faith in Christ, and obedience to him,<sup>z</sup> but infants descending from parents, either both, or but one of them, professing faith in Christ, and obedience to him, are in that respect within the covenant, and to be baptized.<sup>a</sup>

Q.167.ans: The needful but much neglected duty of improving our bap- tism, is to be performed by us all our life long, especially in the time of temptation, and when we are present at the administration of it to others;<sup>b</sup> by serious and thankful consideration of the nature of it, and of the ends for which Christ instituted it, the privileges and benefits conferred and sealed thereby, and our solemn vow made therein;<sup>c</sup> by being humbled for our sinful defilement, our falling short of, and walking contrary to, the grace of baptism, and our engagements;<sup>d</sup> by growing up to assurance of pardon of sin, and of all other blessings sealed to us in that sacrament;<sup>e</sup> by drawing strength from the death and resurrection of Christ, into whom we are baptized, for the mor- tifying of sin, and quickening of grace;<sup>f</sup> and by endeavoring to live by faith,<sup>g</sup> to have our conversation in holiness and righteousness,<sup>h</sup> as those that have therein given up their names to Christ;<sup>i</sup> and to walk in brotherly love, as being baptized by the same Spirit into one body.<sup>k</sup>

Q.168.ans: The Lord’s Supper is a sacrament of the new testament,<sup>l</sup> wherein, by giving and receiving bread and wine according to the appointment of Jesus Christ, his death is showed forth; and they that worthily communicate feed upon his body and blood, to their spiri- tual nourishment and growth in grace;<sup>m</sup> have their union and com- munion with him confirmed;<sup>n</sup> testify and renew their thankfulness,<sup>o</sup> and engagement to God,<sup>p</sup> and their mutual love and fellowship each with other, as members of the same mystical body.<sup>q</sup>

Q.169.ans: Christ hath appointed the ministers of his Word, in the ad- ministration of this sacrament of the Lord’s Supper, to set apart the bread and wine from common use, by the word of institution, thanks- giving, and prayer; to take and break the bread, and to give both the bread and the wine to the communicants: who are, by the same ap- pointment, to take and eat the bread, and to drink the wine, in thankful remembrance that the body of Christ was broken and given, and his blood shed, for them.<sup>r</sup>

Q.170.ans: As the body and blood of Christ are not corporally or car- nally present in, with, or under the bread and wine in the Lord’s Supper,<sup>s</sup> and yet are spiritually present to the faith of the receiver, no less truly and really than the elements themselves are to their out- ward senses;<sup>t</sup> so they that worthily communicate in the sacrament of the Lord’s Supper, do therein feed upon the body and blood of Christ, not after a corporal and carnal, but in a spiritual manner; yet truly and really,<sup>u</sup> while by faith they receive and apply unto themselves Christ crucified, and all the benefits of his death.<sup>w</sup>

Q.171.ans: They that receive the sacrament of the Lord’s Supper are, before they come, to prepare themselves thereunto, by examining themselves<sup>x</sup> of their being in Christ,<sup>y</sup> of their sins and wants;<sup>z</sup> of the truth and measure of their knowledge,<sup>a</sup> faith,<sup>b</sup> repentance;<sup>c</sup> love to God and the brethren,<sup>d</sup> charity to all men,<sup>e</sup> forgiving those that have done them wrong;<sup>f</sup> of their desires after Christ,<sup>g</sup> and of their new obedience;<sup>h</sup> and by renewing the exercise of these graces,<sup>i</sup> by serious meditation,<sup>k</sup> and fervent prayer.<sup>l</sup>

Q.172.ans: One who doubteth of his being in Christ, or of his due prepa- ration to the sacrament of the Lord’s Supper, may have true interest in Christ, though he be not yet assured thereof;<sup>m</sup> and in God’s ac- count hath it, if he be duly affected with the apprehension of the want of it,<sup>n</sup> and unfeignedly desires to be found in Christ,<sup>o</sup> and to depart from iniquity:<sup>p</sup> in which case (because promises are made, and this sacrament is appointed, for the relief even of weak and doubt- ing Christians<sup>q</sup> ) he is to bewail his unbelief,<sup>r</sup> and labor to have his doubts resolved;<sup>s</sup> and, so doing, he may and ought to come to the Lord’s Supper, that he may be further strengthened.<sup>t</sup>

Q.173.ans: Such as are found to be ignorant or scandalous, notwithstand- ing their profession of the faith, and desire to come to the Lord’s Supper, may and ought to be kept from that sacrament, by the power which Christ hath left in his church,<sup>u</sup> until they receive instruction, and manifest their reformation.<sup>w</sup>

Q.174.ans: It is required of them that receive the sacrament of the Lord’s Supper, that, during the time of the administration of it, with all holy reverence and attention they wait upon God in that ordinance,<sup>x</sup> diligently observe the sacramental elements and actions,<sup>y</sup> heedfully discern the Lord’s body,<sup>z</sup> and affectionately meditate on his death and sufferings,<sup>a</sup> and thereby stir up themselves to a vigorous exercise of their graces;<sup>b</sup> in judging themselves,<sup>c</sup> and sorrowing for sin;<sup>d</sup> in earnest hungering and thirsting after Christ,<sup>e</sup> feeding on him by faith,<sup>f</sup> receiving of his fullness,<sup>g</sup> trusting in his merits,<sup>h</sup> rejoicing in his love,<sup>i</sup> giving thanks for his grace;<sup>k</sup> in renewing of their covenant with God,<sup>l</sup> and love to all the saints.<sup>m</sup>
